To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the risk index shows that HQMs are slightly more risky than conventional materials; (b) the cash flow analysis shows that conventional materials are slightly more profitable; and (c) the risk index and cash flow analysis are not in line, which indicates that there is still a lack of knowledge in this field.
HQM projects have a higher risk index than projects with conventional materials, but a similar risk distribution.
HQMs have a slightly lower financial return than conventional materials but are less risky.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to real estate management and the valuation of sustainable projects.
the development of a risk assessment methodology that integrates sustainability criteria in a real estate cash flow model.
a new approach for the valuation of real estate projects with a focus on sustainability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sustainable materials can have a significant impact on the cash flow valuation of a real estate project and thus on the decision making of developers and investors.
HQMs are a viable option for real estate projects and that the risks associated with them are manageable, but that conventional materials are still preferable in the long term.
sustainable real estate development is not only about the use of green materials but also about the use of innovative materials and the integration of risk analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sustainable real estate projects are not necessarily less risky than conventional ones.
HQMs are not only more expensive, but also more risky.
HQM projects are not necessarily better than conventional projects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
risk and environmental performance are interrelated and should not be treated separately.
the integration of HQMs into real estate projects is not a risk, but rather an investment opportunity.
the integration of environmental and long term risks in real estate projects can improve the decision-making process, and thus increase the competitiveness of real estate projects.
